issues.legal_issue: A dedication of property to provide shelter to religious mendicants and support a religiously associated place of veneration creates a public trust for a section of the public, and the trust may extend to the entire property conveyed.
material_facts: The deed transferred the property to a municipality for public use, continuing its use to provide shelter to ascetics, visitors, and religious mendicants.
The deed recorded the presence of a samadhi on the property.
The beneficiaries were persons interested in the samadhi and religious mendicants, rather than an identifiable private group.
The trust proceedings concerned the property conveyed, not only the buildings on it.
issues.conclusion: The property was held subject to a public religious and charitable trust for an uncertain and fluctuating section of the public, and the trust extended to the entire property.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(13) and 9 of the Bombay Public Trusts Act, a trust for a religious or charitable purpose is a public trust, and a purpose of general public utility may benefit a section of the public. Section 10 provides that a public trust is not void merely because its beneficiaries are unascertained or unascertainable. A religious faith or shared veneration does not prevent beneficiaries from constituting a section of the public: Mahant Ram Saroop Dasji v. S. P. Sahi, [1959] Supp. 2 S.C.R. 583. The deed's terms showed that the trust covered the property, not merely the buildings.

rule.if: public_trust_inquiry and property_dedicated_for_religious_shelter and beneficiaries_form_public_section and dedication_covers_conveyed_property

predicates.public_trust_inquiry: An authority conducts an inquiry to determine whether property is subject to a public trust.
predicates.property_dedicated_for_religious_shelter: A settlor transfers property for continued use to shelter religious mendicants or support a religiously associated place of veneration.
predicates.beneficiaries_form_public_section: The intended beneficiaries are an uncertain or changing body of people connected by a shared religious interest, rather than a fixed private group.
predicates.dedication_covers_conveyed_property: The dedication's terms apply to the property conveyed as a whole, rather than only to buildings on it.

issues.definition: When a public-trust inquiry concerns property dedicated for religious shelter to a section of the public, and the dedication covers the conveyed property, the conveyed property is subject to a public trust.

issues.legal_issue: A municipality that accepts property subject to a trust for a specified public benefit cannot divert it to its own purposes.
material_facts: The settlor transferred the property to the municipality for continued use to shelter religious mendicants.
The municipality accepted the transfer and took possession.
The municipality later used parts of the property for its offices and shops.
issues.conclusion: After accepting the property for the stated purpose, the municipality could not divert it to its own purposes in breach of the trust.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17 of the Bombay District Municipal Act, 1873, placed municipal property under municipal management and control for the purposes of that Act, but neither that Act nor the general law prevented a municipality from accepting a trust for a section of the public. Nor did the Act authorize the municipality to use trust property for its own purposes in breach of the trust.

predicates.municipality_received_property: A municipality receives property from a transferor.
predicates.municipality_accepted_public_benefit_ded: The municipality accepts the property for a specified benefit for a section of the public.
predicates.municipality_used_property_for_own_purpo: The municipality uses the property for its own purposes instead of the accepted public benefit.

issues.definition: If a municipality receives and accepts property for a specified public benefit but uses it for its own purposes, it must honor the accepted dedication.

issues.legal_issue: A judgment in a suit against a trespasser does not bar a later determination of whether the property is subject to a public trust when the trespasser did not represent the trust beneficiaries.
material_facts: The municipality had earlier sued an occupant to recover property he had unlawfully occupied.
The occupant asserted a right to reside there as a religious mendicant, but he was sued as a trespasser, not as a representative of trust beneficiaries.
A later proceeding sought a determination of whether the property was subject to a public trust.
issues.conclusion: The earlier judgment did not operate as res judicata and did not prevent the public-trust determination.
issues.legal_principle: The earlier proceeding concerned the municipality's right to recover possession from an alleged trespasser. Because the defendant was not sued in a representative capacity for the trust beneficiaries, that judgment did not determine the public-trust issue or bar its determination in an appropriate proceeding.

predicates.prior_possession_suit_against_trespasser: A property holder earlier sues an occupant to recover possession on the ground that the occupant is a trespasser.
predicates.defendant_not_representing_beneficiaries: The occupant is not sued as a representative of the persons who may benefit from a trust over the property.
predicates.later_public_trust_inquiry: A later proceeding asks an authority to determine whether the property is subject to a public trust.

issues.definition: When a later public-trust inquiry follows a possession suit against an occupant who did not represent the beneficiaries, the earlier judgment does not bar the inquiry.

issues.legal_issue: A survey determination recognizing municipal ownership does not bar a public-trust inquiry that does not challenge the municipality's legal ownership or seek relief inconsistent with the survey determination.
material_facts: A survey officer recorded the municipality as owner of the property and found that it was not a trustee for the claimed community.
The later proceeding sought a declaration that the property was subject to a public trust.
The municipality's legal ownership was not challenged in that proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The survey determination did not bar the public-trust proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: Section 50-A(2) of the Bombay District Municipal Act, 1901, requires dismissal of a suit brought to set aside a covered survey order, or seeking relief inconsistent with that order, subject to the provision's stated conditions. The public-trust proceeding did neither: it left the municipality's legal ownership unchallenged and sought recognition of a trust burden on the property.

rule.if: survey_order_records_municipal_ownership and later_public_trust_inquiry and legal_ownership_unchallenged and relief_consistent_with_survey_order

predicates.survey_order_records_municipal_ownership: A survey authority records a municipality as the owner of property.
predicates.later_public_trust_inquiry: A later proceeding asks an authority to determine whether the property is subject to a public trust.
predicates.legal_ownership_unchallenged: The later proceeding does not contest the municipality's legal ownership of the property.
predicates.relief_consistent_with_survey_order: The relief sought in the later proceeding does not set aside or conflict with the survey authority's ownership determination.

issues.definition: When a later public-trust inquiry leaves municipal ownership unchallenged and seeks relief consistent with the survey order, that order does not bar the inquiry.

issues.legal_issue: In a public-trust inquiry initiated by an interested person, the authority may declare and register a public trust for beneficiaries different from those identified in the application if the inquiry establishes that the trust exists.
material_facts: An interested applicant sought a declaration that the property was held for a particular community and requested registration as a public trust.
The inquiry found that the property was held for the benefit of a different section of the public interested in the samadhi.
The authority found that a public trust existed.
issues.conclusion: The authority could declare the public trust and make consequential orders consistent with its findings even though the applicant's asserted beneficiary group was not established.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 18 and 19 of the Bombay Public Trusts Act permit an inquiry to begin on an application under section 18, on an application by a person interested in a public trust, or on the authority's own motion. Under section 19, the inquiry determines whether a public trust exists; if it does, the authority must declare and register it notwithstanding the particular claim made by the applicant.

predicates.public_trust_inquiry_started_by_interest: A person claiming an interest in a public trust initiates an inquiry into the property or trust.
predicates.applicant_identifies_specific_beneficiar: The applicant asserts that the trust benefits a particular group of people.
predicates.inquiry_finds_different_public_beneficia: The inquiry finds that the trust benefits a public group different from the group asserted by the applicant.
predicates.inquiry_finds_public_trust: The authority conducting the inquiry finds that a public trust exists.

issues.definition: If an interested applicant initiates an inquiry asserting particular beneficiaries, but the inquiry finds a public trust for different public beneficiaries, the authority may declare and register the trust for those found beneficiaries.

issues.legal_issue: A charity commissioner who is a party and is interested in the due administration of trust property may appeal an adverse judicial decision concerning the existence of a public trust.
material_facts: The charity commissioner had determined at an earlier stage that a public trust existed.
A court later set aside that determination and found that no public trust existed.
The charity commissioner was a party to the appeal and sought to support the earlier determination.
issues.conclusion: The charity commissioner was entitled to appeal the adverse decision, notwithstanding that the appeal supported the view previously reached in a quasi-judicial capacity.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Bombay Public Trusts Act directs the charity commissioner to superintend the administration of the Act and carry out its provisions. Section 72 provides for the relevant court proceeding. A person interested in the due administration of property and made a party to the proceeding cannot be denied a right of appeal merely because that person supports a view previously reached in a quasi-judicial capacity.

rule.if: public_trust_court_proceeding and commissioner_is_party and commissioner_has_administration_interest and decision_is_adverse_to_trust_finding

predicates.public_trust_court_proceeding: A court considers a proceeding concerning whether property is subject to a public trust.
predicates.commissioner_is_party: The official responsible for overseeing public trusts is a party to the court proceeding.
predicates.commissioner_has_administration_interest: The official has an interest in the due administration of the property and the applicable trust regime.
predicates.decision_is_adverse_to_trust_finding: The court reaches a decision contrary to the official's position that a public trust exists.

issues.definition: In a court proceeding about a public trust, an interested trust official who is a party may appeal a decision adverse to the finding that a trust exists.
